expectations.text: Exactly one SPECS.md and one RUBRIC.md were produced (no v1/v2 or side-by-side alternates)
expectations.evidence: Files are named spec.md and rubric.md, not SPECS.md/RUBRIC.md.

expectations.text: SPECS.md contains all required sections: Purpose, Trigger conditions, Inputs, Outputs, Scope & boundaries, Non-goals, Edge cases, Open assumptions
expectations.evidence: Has Scope, Input Assumptions, Output Format, Edge Cases, Non-Goals — but no dedicated Trigger conditions section, and 'Open Questions (for David, before build)' covers deferred questions, not stated assumptions.

expectations.text: SPECS.md content is specific to meeting-notes-to-action-items (not generic boilerplate)
expectations.evidence: Includes a worked example against a real sample and a 3-way line classification scheme.

expectations.text: Every RUBRIC.md criterion has a 0-3 scale with concrete, spec-grounded per-level descriptions, and criterion 1 is triggering accuracy
expectations.evidence: Uses a 1-5 scale (not 0-3) plus separate hard-fail gates; scored criteria are recall/precision/owner attribution/due-date/phrasing/dedup/format/usability — no triggering-accuracy criterion at all.

expectations.text: RUBRIC.md has 6-12 criteria plus a scoring summary table with band cutoffs correctly computed against this run's actual max
expectations.evidence: 8 scored criteria (within range) plus 2 separate hard-fail gates, but on a 1-5 scale rather than 0-3, with a pass-threshold summary rather than the specified banded table format.

expectations.text: Transcript shows a self-evaluation pass (Step 5) happening before the documents are presented as final
expectations.evidence: No adversarial self-check described; documents delivered directly after the Q&A round.

expectations.text: Transcript shows at least one round of simulated user feedback followed by a revision (Step 6 loop actually exercised)
